title: workspace trust is a Build toggle and one Bash answer covers the workspace
intent: The user still saw Build ask before every Bash command. The cause was exact-rule memory: the request resource of Bash is the command text, so Allow for this session remembered one command. The wave makes workspace trust a separate Build toggle instead of a fourth mode. With the toggle on, one remembered answer covers later work inside the session directory. A Bash answer carries a separate workspace-shell grant named by the session root, so one answer covers later Bash commands started there; paths outside the root still ask. The ACP catalog returns Plan, Build and Auto plus the workspaceTrust boolean.
checks: cd plugin/yeah-provider && npm run typecheck && npm test
objection: The shell grant is a permission grant, not a sandbox: after the person allows Bash in the workspace, a command can address the machine with the user's rights. The boundary checks the tool's declared directory and named paths; it cannot enumerate every way a shell command may name a path. The ACP config option exposes the toggle, but whether every orchestrator renders booleans is a client question.
refuted_by: Build asks again for a different Bash command in the same directory after Allow for this session/project/global, the grant covers a path declared outside the session directory, or turning workspaceTrust off does not restore per-call Build questions
note: Targeted offline checks pass: byte-compilation, 468 ERT tests, wire mode check, scope check, TypeScript check and 70 plugin tests. A live ACP probe against GLM-5.3-Flash publishes Build, three modes, and workspaceTrust=true; it stops at the expected first Bash permission because its scripted client cannot answer.
